root_causes: Native targeted messages to embedded own extension frames were not delivered, although runtime messages worked.
Embedded own extension frames could not fetch already-granted HTTP media while top-level extension/background could.
WebKit exposes a serviceWorker container on extension documents but rejects registration except HTTP/HTTPS. Genuine document worker registration rejection retained in35.
Chrome package uses its non-Chrome save path without declaring downloads. Narrow generated-document save does not grant network/history APIs.
Native helper cannot read an iframe-partitioned extension Blob. Real owner-frame <a download> initiates WebKit download; native queue is then associated with owning extension.

Production runtime started only a subset of background types while earlier audit helpers explicitly started backgrounds. Normal loading now awaits all declared backgrounds and concurrent loads join the same pending task.

Restored module worker could report loaded without responsive publisher message listeners. Module compatibility bootstrap now uses a native nonpersistent module event page with the original publisher import graph; stable extension identity, permissions and settings preserved. Changing only worker wrapper filename failed and was reverted.

limitations: userScripts messaging:true and execute are unsupported; complex CSP is rejected; top-level cross-registration global bindings are not shared. Not all Chrome APIs/extensions are claimed compatible.
Intermittent reported self-closing was not reproduced in the actual three-round reload/disable/enable audit; no blanket guarantee for arbitrary extensions or future publisher revisions.
